methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $18M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Dendra Systems is a Series A-stage climate and energy company that has raised $18M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the narrow peer set at Dendra's stage and valuation tier yielded insufficient data points for a reliable peer-median analysis.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable here. Using total raised ($18M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, this method implies a valuation of $36M. The peer-median method was not applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector meeting our criteria; relying on the full sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the wide dispersion in company profiles and capital intensity.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $31M (low) to $41M (high), with a median of $36M. The range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of the 2.0x step-up assumption absent market comps, the composition and stage distribution of the Climate & Energy peer universe, and whether total raised is an appropriate proxy for post-money valuation at Series A. A peer-comparable analysis becomes viable once more narrow-stage data accumulates in this sector.
